blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en:
Robustness verification is essential for ensuring the safety and security of neural networks, but current methods focus heavily on
  norm-ball attacks, which do not adequately model typical real-world threats that present physical perturbations, known as patch attacks. A naive approach requires computationally prohibitive enumeration of all possible patch positions. To address the challenge, we propose a novel neural network verification method specialized to the patch-attack threat. Instead of enumerating patch locations, we first model the patch attack with group-wise sparsity and formulate its verification methods as a mixed-integer semidefinite program (MISDP) by applying SDP relaxation to the neural network. We then propose three relaxations, including Group-Lasso relaxation, that remove the integer variables while preserving the sparse, group-wise structure of the original attack, enabling substantially efficient verification. Our empirical analysis demonstrates that the proposed relaxations require less than 3% of the computation time of the original MISDP, while the Group-Lasso relaxation incurs only a 0.34\% average increase in the objective value over the original formulation. Furthermore, Group-Lasso achieves a verified rate of 91%, compared with under 70% for prior methods.

blocks.en: Deep Neural Networks (DNNs) have achieved remarkable success in many fields and have been widely deployed in safety-critical vision applications such as autonomous driving [ 4 , 24 ] and medical image analysis [ 11 , 33 ] . However, DNNs are widely known to be vulnerable to adversarial attacks [ 29 , 14 , 8 ] that intentionally modify an input with subtle malicious perturbations to induce an incorrect prediction. The vulnerability to adversarial attacks has raised critical concerns about their reliability and security, spurring extensive research into DNN verification [ 30 , 32 , 10 , 15 ] .
blocks.zh: 深神经网络(DNNs)在许多领域取得了显著成功,并被广泛应用于安全关键视觉应用,如自主驾驶[4,24]和医疗图像分析[11,33]. 然而,众所周知,DNNs容易受到对抗性攻击[29,14,8],这种攻击有意用微妙的恶意扰动修改输入,以诱导不正确的预测. 对抗性攻击的脆弱性引起了人们对其可靠性和安全性的严重关切,激发了对DNN核查的广泛研究[30、32、10、15]。

blocks.en: DNN verification has traditionally focused on L p L_{p} norm-ball attacks. For an input image 𝒙 ∗ \bm{x}^{\ast} , the verifier considers all possible perturbed images 𝒙 \bm{x} under a perturbation radius ϵ \epsilon , i.e., ‖ 𝒙 − 𝒙 ∗ ‖ p ≤ ϵ ||\bm{x}-\bm{x}^{\ast}||_{p}\leq\epsilon , and determines whether the model prediction remains unchanged. This verification problem is generally solved as an optimization problem. While the L p L_{p} norm-ball assumption can cover broader types of perturbations, it does not adequately represent the threat model of practical physical-world attacks [ 28 , 6 ] in which an attacker modifies only a localized region, for example by attaching a sticker or placing a patterned object on part of an image. A naive approach to patch attacks enumerates possible patch locations and solves a verification problem for each candidate location, but the computational cost grows exponentially with the number of possible attack locations.

blocks.en:
To address this limitation, we propose a novel DNN verification method specialized for patch attacks. Instead of enumerating patch locations, we model the patch attack with group-wise sparsity [ 12 ] . We then incorporate the patch position as a variable within a single mixed-integer program (MIP), which is an exact model but is not practical due to its high combinatorial complexity.
We thus relax the problem with an SDP relaxation [ 16 ] and three proposed relaxations for the group-wise patch attack.
We propose a full-group naive relaxation that permits perturbations in every group, an L 2 L_{2} -norm relaxation that replaces the group-wise constraints with a global L 2 L_{2} constraint, and a Group-Lasso relaxation that constrains the sum of the L 2 L_{2} norms of the group-wise perturbations. All three relaxed problems provide a valid guarantee for the original attack model.

因此,我们放松了SDP放松[16]的问题,并提出了三条针对分组补丁攻击的放松.

blocks.en:
We evaluate the proposed formulations from both computational and verification perspectives. We found that all three relaxations require less than 3% of the computation time of the original problem in the evaluated settings. Group-Lasso relaxation achieves an average objective increase of only 0.34% in the evaluated setting, substantially outperforming the Full-Group and L 2 L_{2} -norm relaxations. These results indicate that preserving the group structure of the attack is important for obtaining a tight relaxation. Group-Lasso relaxation also demonstrated high verification capability; while existing methods achieve verification rates of ≤ \leq 70%, it was able to verify 91% of the samples on the adversarially trained model.
We conduct qualitative analysis and confirm that the perturbations considered in Group-Lasso relaxation are locally grouped and concentrated around the digit character, as shown in Fig. 1 .

blocks.en: Our main contributions are summarized as follows: • We are the first to formulate DNN verification specialized for patch attacks with group-wise sparsity modeling. We first formulate it as an exact MIP problem and design an effective relaxation enabling efficient verification. • We design three relaxations for the group-wise modeling with theoretical soundness guarantees. In particular, Group-Lasso relaxation explicitly preserves the group-sparse structure and provides a substantially tighter approximation than the simpler relaxations. • We demonstrate the high efficiency and effectiveness of our proposed methods, which require at most 3% of the computation time of the original MISDP. Group-Lasso relaxation differs from the exact formulation by only 0.34% in objective value and achieves a verification rate of up to 91%, outperforming existing methods, whose verification rates are at most 70%.

blocks.zh: 2 相关工作

blocks.en: 2.1 Adversarial Attacks
blocks.zh: 2.1 横向攻击

blocks.en: Deep Neural Networks (DNNs) are widely known to be vulnerable to adversarial attacks [ 29 , 14 , 8 ] , where carefully crafted perturbations alter model predictions while remaining imperceptible to humans. To bound perturbation magnitude, traditional attacks are typically formulated within an L p L_{p} -norm ball, such as L ∞ L_{\infty} [ 21 ] or L 2 L_{2} [ 8 ] balls.
blocks.zh: 深神经网络(DNNs)广为人知,容易受到对抗性攻击[29,14,8],其中精心设计的扰动会改变模型预测,同时对人类仍然无法察觉. 传统攻击通常在L p _{p 范围内进行。 - 诺姆球,例如LQQL_{\infty}[21]或L2L_{2}[8]球。

blocks.en:
Beyond global perturbation, recent work has demonstrated that effective attacks can be realized by perturbing only a localized region of the input image [ 19 , 28 , 27 ] . We refer to this threat model as patch attacks .
Attacks based on L p L_{p} norm balls perturb the entire image, which would require physically perturbing everything within the camera’s field of view, an unrealistic requirement in the physical world. An attacker would therefore need to compromise the system itself. In contrast, patch attacks allow an adversary to introduce localized physical perturbations by placing patches within the camera’s field of view [ 6 , 26 ] or attaching stickers to target objects [ 28 ] , without compromising the system. Owing to this practicality in real-world scenarios, patch attacks have drawn significant attention.
blocks.zh:
除了全球扰动外,最近的研究表明,只有扰动输入图像的局部区域[19、28、27],才能实现有效的攻击。 我们称这个威胁模式为补丁攻击。
基于 L p L_{p} 规范球 扰动整个图像, 这需要物理扰动 摄像头视野内的一切, 因此,攻击者需要损害系统本身。 反之,补丁攻击则允许对手通过将补丁放置在相机视野内[6,26]或者在目标物体上附贴[28]来引入局部物理扰动,而不影响系统. 由于现实世界情景中的这种实用性,补丁攻击引起了很大关注.

blocks.en: This emerging threat model has motivated the development of certified defenses against patch attacks [ 9 , 35 , 34 , 17 , 22 ] . Chiang et al. [ 9 ] proposed a certified defense that enumerates possible patch locations and performs verification for each location. Levine et al. [ 17 ] developed a deterministic certification approach that restricts the set of possible patch regions and verifies the resulting cases. BagCert [ 22 ] avoids explicit enumeration of all patch locations by partitioning the input image into multiple regions and performing certified defense for CNNs. However, existing approaches focus on developing certified defenses, not verification for all possible attacks. None of the prior studies has studied DNN verification methods specialized for patch attacks. This gap motivates our study.
blocks.zh: 这种新兴的威胁模式促使开发了针对补丁攻击的认证防御[9,35,34,17,22]. 蒋等. [9] 提出了经认证的辩护,列举可能的补丁位置并对每个位置进行核查。 莱文等人著. [17] 开发了一种确定性认证方法,限制一套可能的补丁区域并核实由此产生的案例。 BagCert [22] 避免通过将输入图像分割成多个区域,为CNN进行认证防御来明确列出所有补丁位置. 然而,现有方法侧重于开发认证防御,而不是对所有可能的攻击进行核查. 以往的研究都没有研究过DNN用于补丁攻击的核查方法. 这一差距促使我们进行研究。

blocks.en: DNN verification has been studied through both complete and incomplete verification approaches. Complete verification [ 10 , 20 , 5 , 15 , 30 , 2 ] seeks to solve Problem Eq. 1 exactly, typically using mixed-integer programming (MIP) [ 30 , 32 ] or satisfiability modulo theories (SMT) [ 10 , 15 ] . Although these methods can provide exact verification, their computational cost is generally unaffordable for practical use.
blocks.zh: 通过完整和不完整的核查方法研究了DNN核查。 完整的核查[10, 20, 5, 15, 30, 2] 力求精确地解决问题 Eq. 1, 通常使用混合整数编程(MIP)[30, 32] 或相容性调制理论(SMT)[10, 15]. 虽然这些方法可以提供准确的核实,但其计算成本一般无法实际使用.

blocks.en: Incomplete verification instead replaces the original verification problem with a relaxed problem that is computationally more tractable. The relaxed problem is constructed as a necessary condition for the original verification problem: consequently, if the relaxed problem is verified, then the original DNN verification problem is also verified. However, this relaxation can introduce false negatives, meaning that a model may be certifiably robust under complete verification even when the incomplete verifier fails to establish robustness.
blocks.zh: 不完全的核查代替原先的核查问题,取而代之的是一个较宽松的问题,从计算上讲,这个问题比较容易拉动。 放松问题被构建为原始核查问题的必要条件:因此,如果放松问题得到核实,那么最初的DNN核查问题也得到核实。 然而,这种放松可能引入虚假的负面效果,也就是说,即使不完全的核查者未能建立稳健性,在全面核查下,一个模型也可能是可证明有效的。

The MISDP ( 9 ) eliminates the binary variables associated with the ReLU activations, but retains the binary attack-selection variable 𝑮 \bm{G} . This remaining combinatorial structure still limits the scalability of the verification problem.

Thus, Group-Lasso provides a tighter relaxation than the L 2 L_{2} -norm relaxation while explicitly retaining the group structure of the original attack.
After replacing the original perturbation set 𝒳 \mathcal{X} with any of the three convex sets above, the binary variable 𝑮 \bm{G} is no longer required. This removes the combinatorial optimization over attack locations and enables substantially more scalable verification of larger neural networks.

blocks.en: We evaluate the proposed relaxation methods from three perspectives: computational efficiency, relaxation tightness, and verification performance.

blocks.en:
All experiments were conducted on a node with two AMD EPYC 9654 CPUs (96 cores per socket, up to 3707 MHz) and 768 GiB of memory. To solve the MISDP, we used SCIP-SDP [ 3 ] with SoPlex [ 13 ] to handle the branch-and-bound framework required for solving the auxiliary LPs. For our methods, we used MOSEK [ 23 ] to solve the relaxed SDPs.
The image is partitioned into non-overlapping square groups using a sliding window, where the side length of each square group specifies the group size. When the side length of the image is not evenly divisible by the group size, the remaining pixels are grouped together as a single group.

blocks.en: 4.4 Verification Rate Comparison

blocks.en: We evaluate the verification rates of the proposed relaxations, comparing them with prior verification methods in addition to the relaxation tightness comparison in Sec. 4.3 .
blocks.zh: 我们评价提议的放松的核查率,除了第4.3节的放松紧凑性比较之外,还要与以前的核查方法进行比较。

blocks.en:
We follow the evaluation methodology adopted in prior work [ 18 ] to facilitate comparison with existing verification methods. We evaluate two fully connected architectures, FCNNa and FCNNb. FCNNa consists of two hidden layers with width 20, while FCNNb consists of three hidden layers with width 100.
For both FCNNa and FCNNb, the input layer dimension matches the total number of pixels in the input image, which is 784 for MNIST in our case.
For each architecture, we consider both normally trained ( Clean ) and PGD-adversarially trained ( Adv. ) models. The adversarially trained models are trained using PGD with the perturbation radius specified by the corresponding setting.
For each setting, we evaluate 100 test samples, selected at indices 0,100 , 0,100, .. , 9900 ,9900 .
The verification rate is the fraction of samples for which the verification optimization certifies that the model remains robust against the specified target class under the corresponding perturbation set.
We compare the proposed Full-Group, L 2 L_{2} -norm, and Group-Lasso relaxations against bounded-MILP [ 30 ] , CROWN-IBP [ 36 ] , and CROWN [ 37 ] . The attack cardinality k k is 1, partitioning the input into 4 4 -pixel groups.
These baselines are representative L p L_{p} -norm-based verification methods and include the state-of-the-art methods reported in [ 18 ] .

blocks.en: We qualitatively examine the perturbations obtained from the optimization solutions. This analysis provides an intuitive comparison between the perturbations produced by the proposed group-wise threat model and those produced by conventional L p L_{p} -based verification methods.
blocks.zh: 我们从质量上审查了从优化解决方案中获得的干扰。 这一分析可直观地比较拟议的分组威胁模型产生的干扰和传统的L p _{p 型核查方法产生的干扰。

blocks.en:
For bounded MILP, we directly use the optimal solution, as it is complete verification.
For incomplete verification, which only tests the upper bound of the objective value and does not return attack perturbations, we construct approximated attack perturbations using the following procedure.
For IBP perturbations, we determine the perturbation direction for each pixel based on its sensitivity to the true and target label scores, computed via forward propagation, and obtain an approximate perturbation by moving as far as possible in that direction within the input perturbation bound.
For SDP-based methods including ours, we extract the sub-vector corresponding to the original image and reshape it back into the original image’s 2D array. Specifically, the sub-vector extracted corresponds to entries [0,1] through [0,256] of the SDP solution.
blocks.zh:
对于有界限的MILP,我们直接使用最佳解决方案,因为它是完整的核查.
为了进行不完全的核查,仅测试目标值的上限,而不返回攻击扰动,我们采用以下程序构建大约攻击扰动.
对于IBP扰动,我们根据其对真实和目标标签分数的敏感度确定每个像素的扰动方向,通过前向传播计算,并在输入扰动约束范围内尽可能向该方向移动,从而获得大致扰动.
对于基于SDP的方法,包括我们的,我们提取与原始图像相对应的子播放器,并将其重塑为原始图像的2D阵列. 具体地说,提取的子向量对应SDP解决方案的[0,1]至[0,256]条目.

blocks.en:
Figure 3 shows the perturbations obtained for an input image whose true label is 7, shown in Fig. 1 , with target class 0, in a setting where Group-Lasso successfully verifies the model. All methods attempt to suppress or modify the digit 7. However, Group-Lasso relaxation concentrates the perturbation almost entirely on the digit itself, leaving the surrounding background unchanged. This behavior is consistent with the assumed localized patch threat model.
In contrast, the perturbations obtained by the other methods extend into the background region. In particular, the perturbations produced by IBP and MILP distribute non-negligible changes outside the digit region. The proposed Full-Group and L 2 L_{2} -norm relaxations reduce this effect compared with these baselines, but still permit perturbations outside the localized region. These observations illustrate the benefit of explicitly retaining group sparsity in the perturbation set.

与此相反,其他方法获得的扰动延伸到背景区域。 特别是,IBP和MILP产生的扰动将不可忽略的变化分布在数字区域之外. 拟议的Guart-Group和L 2 L_{2}-规范放松与这些基线相比减少了这种影响,但仍允许在本地化区域之外进行干扰。 这些意见表明,在扰动装置中明确保留群体痉挛的好处。

blocks.en: Figure 4 shows an instance with true label 2, shown in Fig. 1 , and target class 0 for which Group-Lasso does not certify robustness. Fig. 5 shows the corresponding reconstructed images. In this case, the perturbations produced by most methods modify both the digit and the surrounding background. Group-Lasso not only concentrates its perturbation on the digit region, but also tries to draw the target digit, 0. This supports the high capability of Group-Lasso to handle the patch attack, which can only inject localized perturbations. When subtle perturbations are insufficient, it is natural that the attacker instead draws the target digit.

blocks.en: In summary, the qualitative results support the motivation for the proposed relaxation: Group-Lasso not only provides a substantially tighter relaxation than the simpler alternatives, but also produces optimization solutions whose perturbations are spatially concentrated in a manner consistent with the assumed patch attack.
blocks.zh: 总而言之,质量结果支持了提议放松的动机: Group-Lasso公司不仅比更简单的替代品提供大幅更严格的放松,而且还产生优化解决方案,其扰动空间集中的方式与假设的补丁攻击一致.

blocks.en: 5 Discussion and Limitations
blocks.zh: 5 讨论和限制

blocks.en:
The results highlight the importance of preserving the spatial structure of patch threats during verification. Among the proposed relaxations, Group-Lasso consistently provides the tightest approximation to the original MISDP and effectively concentrates perturbations within targeted regions, leading to stronger robustness certification against patch attacks.
However, there are several limitations in this study. We evaluated only fully connected networks and small-scale inputs, leaving high-resolution images and modern architectures for future work. Our primary focus is the theoretical formulation of patch attacks ( Sec. 3 ) and the tightness of the proposed relaxations relative to the original MISDP, which is itself unsuitable for large-scale problems. As the first formal verification framework specialized for patch attacks, we leave the development of scalable solvers, such as first-order methods [ 1 , 7 ] , to future work. Finally, our fixed, non-overlapping image partition may not effectively capture arbitrary physical patch geometries. Nevertheless, it can flexibly incorporate realistic deployable regions, which are naturally constrained in physical settings (e.g., stickers cannot be placed on the sky).
blocks.zh:
结果突出了在核查期间保持补丁威胁空间结构的重要性。 在拟议的放松措施中,Group-Lasso一直为最初的MISP提供最紧凑的近似效果,并有效地将扰动集中在目标区域内,从而导致更强有力的防补丁攻击认证.
然而,本研究有一些局限性。 我们只评价了完全连接的网络和小规模的投入,将高分辨率的图像和现代建筑留给今后的工作。 我们的主要焦点是补丁攻击(第3条)的理论表述,以及相对于最初的MISDP而拟议的放松的紧凑性,它本身不适合大规模问题. 作为第一个专门处理补丁攻击的正式核查框架,我们把发展可伸缩的解析器,例如一阶方法[1,7]留待未来工作. 最后,我们固定的、非重叠的图像分区可能无法有效捕捉任意的物理补丁几何。 尽管如此,它可以灵活地纳入现实的可部署区域,这些区域自然在物理环境中受到限制(例如,贴纸不能贴在天空上)。

blocks.en: 6 Conclusion
blocks.zh: 6 结论

blocks.en: In this work, we introduced a one-shot framework for robustness verification against patch attacks. Instead of enumerating possible attack locations, we formulated the attack location jointly with the adversarial perturbation and derived an exact mixed-integer semidefinite programming formulation. We then eliminated the discrete attack-selection variables through three convex relaxations: Full-Group, L 2 L_{2} -norm, and Group-Lasso. Our analyses demonstrate that explicitly preserving the spatial group-sparsity of real-world threats is critical for effective verification. Group-Lasso relaxation provides a tight and efficient approximation, incurring only a 0.34% average increase in the objective value compared to the original MISDP while requiring less than 3% of the computation time. Furthermore, by achieving a verification rate of 91% compared to ≤ \leq 70% for prior baselines, our approach offers a practical, scalable solution for certifying neural network robustness. Future work will explore extending this framework to broader classes of physical attacks and larger network architectures.
blocks.zh: 在这项工作中,我们引入了一个一弹一弹的框架,用于对补丁攻击进行有力核查。 我们没有列举可能的攻击地点,而是将攻击地点与对抗性的扰动结合起来,并得出精确的混合式半固定编程公式。 然后,我们通过三个对流放松来消除离散的攻击选择变量:Full-Group,L 2 L_{2} -Norm,以及Group-Lasso. 我们的分析表明,明确维护现实世界威胁的空间群体分布对有效核查至关重要。 Group-Lasso放松提供了紧凑高效的近似效果,与最初的MISDP相比,目标值平均只增加0.34%,同时需要不到3%的计算时间. 此外,通过实现91%的核查率,而前一个基线的核查率为 \ leq 70%,我们的方法为验证神经网络的稳健性提供了一个切实可行的、可扩展的解决方案。 今后的工作将探讨将这一框架扩大到更广泛的物理攻击类别和更大的网络架构。
